Pull-down and pull-out kitchen faucets from Moen, Delta, Gerber, Grohe, hansgrohe, Pfister, Brizo, Matco-Norca, Franke, Peerless, American Standard, Elkay and Rohl. They are single-handle faucets at 1.5 or 1.75 gpm, in polished chrome, stainless, matte black, oil rubbed bronze, champagne bronze and brushed gold. A pull-down faucet has a tall arc and a sprayer that comes straight down into the bowl. A pull-out faucet has a lower spout and a sprayer that comes toward you, which suits a sink under a window or a low upper cabinet. Moen models include Align, Brantford, Sleek and Camerist, with Reflex docking and Power Clean or Power Boost spray; Gerber uses SnapBack retraction; Grohe Concetto and Delta Emmeline are also listed. Spray patterns run from a single stream to dual and triple spray.

How to choose

  • Arc and clearance: measure from the deck to whatever is above it. A pull-down needs headroom; a pull-out fits under a window or low cabinet.
  • Hole count: a single-handle faucet needs one hole. On a three-hole sink, add a deck plate if one is not in the box.
  • Flow rate: faucets here are 1.5 or 1.75 gpm; check the limit where you install.
  • Finish: stainless-look finishes have different names by brand and do not match each other exactly.
  • Spout reach: compare the reach with the bowl position, especially on double-bowl sinks.

Pull-down and pull-out faucets in detail

Pull-down or pull-out is decided by the sink and the wall behind it, not by the faucet. A pull-down has a tall arc and the sprayer comes straight down into the bowl — it wants headroom, and it is the right answer over a deep single-bowl sink. A pull-out has a lower spout and the sprayer comes toward you, which is what works under a window, beneath a low upper cabinet, or on a shallow or double-bowl sink where a high arc would just splash. The pull-out also reaches further onto the counter, which matters if you fill pots off the sink rather than in it. Measure the clearance from the deck to whatever is above it before choosing the arc.

Docking and spray features differ by brand. Moen lists Reflex docking and Gerber lists SnapBack retraction; Moen's Power Clean and Power Boost are spray features. When a sprayer sags out of the spout or will not seat, the cause is usually under the sink and not in the head: a hose weight has slid along the hose, or the hose is snagged on a shutoff, a disposal or the trap. Reseat the weight as the manufacturer's instructions show and clear the hose path before replacing anything.

A single-handle faucet needs one hole, and many sinks are drilled for three. A deck plate covers the gap. Some faucets here include one, such as Gerber's G0040164 Viper, which names it in the title, and for the rest it is a separate item. Check the sink's hole count before ordering.

Faucets here are listed at 1.5 or 1.75 gpm. Check the limit that applies where you install.

Stainless-look finishes have different names by brand. Moen calls it Spot Resist Stainless, Delta Arctic Stainless, Grohe SuperSteel and hansgrohe Stainless Steel Optic. They do not match each other exactly, so if the faucet and accessories come from different brands, pick the finish family once.

Bar and prep sinks have their own shorter line in pull-out prep and bar faucets; replacement sprayers and hoses are in faucet parts.

Common questions

What is the difference between a pull-down and a pull-out faucet?

A pull-down has a tall arc and the sprayer comes straight down into the bowl. A pull-out has a lower spout and the sprayer comes toward you, which works under a window or a low upper cabinet.

Will a single-handle kitchen faucet fit a three-hole sink?

Yes, with a deck plate that covers the two unused holes. Some faucets include one; for the rest it is a separate item, so check the listing.

Why does my pull-down sprayer not retract?

The cause is usually under the sink: the counterweight has slid along the hose, or the hose is caught on a shutoff, the disposal or the trap. Reseat the weight as the manufacturer's instructions show and clear the hose path.

Tub and shower trim kits: the handle, escutcheon, tub spout and showerhead that mount on the finished wall over a rough-in valve. Brands include Moen, Delta, Pfister and Gerber. Moen kits cover the Posi-Temp and M-CORE valve families in the Align, Brantford, Eva, Genta LX, Gibson, Glyde, Rizon and Voss lines. How to choose

  • Valve compatibility: identify the valve in the wall before ordering. Trim for a current valve may not fit an older body, even from the same brand.

Common questions

What comes in a tub and shower trim kit?

Usually the handle, the escutcheon plate, the tub spout and the showerhead. Kits marked "no head" or "NH" leave out the showerhead. The rough-in valve is usually sold separately; check the listing.

How do I know which trim kit fits my valve?

Match the brand and valve family. For Moen, a Posi-Temp valve takes Posi-Temp trim and an M-CORE valve takes M-CORE trim of the same series.

What is the difference between a tub/shower trim and a shower-only trim?

A tub/shower kit includes a tub spout with a diverter. A shower-only kit has just the handle, escutcheon and showerhead.

Shower trim kits from Moen, Delta, Pfister, Gerber and Grohe: the handle, escutcheon and showerhead that finish a stand-up shower. A trim set is not a valve. It is the visible half of the assembly, and behind the wall it needs a rough-in valve body, sold separately unless the listing says the valve is included. Trim only fits its own manufacturer's valve family: Moen trim goes on the matching Moen Posi-Temp or M-CORE valve, and Delta trim goes on the Delta MultiChoice rough-in. Finishes are led by chrome, brushed nickel and matte black. If the showerhead is staying and only the handle is being replaced, a valve-only trim is the simpler part.

How to choose

  • Valve compatibility: confirm which rough-in is in the wall. On a remodel it cannot be checked after the tile is up.
  • Flow rate: some states cap shower flow below the federal limit. Check the GPM in the listing.
  • Finish name: brushed nickel, spot resist brushed nickel and stainless are three different finishes. Order the room from one finish name.
  • Handle: lever handles operate without tight grasping, pinching or twisting.
  • Outlets: a shower with more than one outlet needs an in-wall diverter or transfer valve.

Common questions

Does a shower trim kit include the valve?

Usually not. A trim kit is the handle, escutcheon and showerhead. The rough-in valve in the wall is usually sold separately, so check the listing, and the trim must match the valve's brand and family.

What does "shower only" mean on a Moen trim?

It means the kit has no tub spout. It is for a stand-up shower; for a tub and shower combination, see tub-shower trim sets.

Can I replace only the shower handle?

Yes. If the showerhead is staying, a valve-only trim with just the handle and escutcheon is the simpler part.

How to choose

  • Valve compatibility: confirm the valve body in the wall, by manufacturer and series, before ordering the trim.
  • Functions: check how many outlets the trim controls: single, dual or triple function, or volume control with a diverter.
  • Handles: some Brizo trims are supplied less handles; the handle kit is a separate item.
  • Wall depth: note the wall depth range of the valve and whether an extension kit is needed for thicker walls.

Common questions

Does thermostatic trim include the valve?

Listings named "trim" are the visible parts only. The thermostatic rough-in valve is ordered separately and must be the matching valve from the same manufacturer and series.

What is the difference between thermostatic and pressure-balance trim?

A pressure-balance valve holds the hot and cold mix steady when pressure changes. A thermostatic valve holds the outlet temperature itself, which is the usual choice for showers with several outlets. Each takes its own trim.

Shower and tub-shower rough-in valves: the valve body that goes in the wall before it closes, in pressure-balance, thermostatic and multi-outlet configurations. Brands include Moen, Delta, Grohe, Brizo, Rohl, American Standard and DXV. Moen M-PACT Posi-Temp and M-CORE valves are listed by connection type; Delta and Brizo MultiChoice Universal rough-ins, Grohe pressure balance rough-ins and the American Standard and DXV Flash rough-in are also here. The rough-in and the finish trim are two separate purchases, so the valve can be set during construction and the finish chosen later. The two must belong to the same manufacturer family: a Moen trim will not fit a Delta body, and cartridge families change between generations within a brand. A pressure-balance valve holds the hot-cold ratio when pressure drops elsewhere; a thermostatic valve holds the outlet temperature.

How to choose

  • Valve family: choose the valve for the trim you want. Trim and valve must come from the same manufacturer family.
  • Pressure-balance or thermostatic: pressure-balance suits a single-outlet shower or tub-shower; thermostatic is what a multi-outlet shower needs.
  • Connection type: sweat (CC) for copper, IPS for threaded pipe, or crimp ring or cold-expansion PEX. Universal bodies accept more than one.
  • Integral stops: check whether the body includes stops. Without them, servicing the cartridge means shutting off the whole house.
  • Outlets: a shower with more than one outlet needs a diverter or transfer valve.

Shower valve replacement

If a shower drips, runs too hot or too cold, or the handle is stiff, the fix is usually the cartridge, not the whole valve. Replace the valve body when it is corroded, leaking inside the wall, or not pressure-balanced. Staying with the same brand and valve family keeps your trim options open and can limit how much tile you need to open. Find cartridges in tub and shower repair parts, and match the finish with shower trim sets, tub-shower trim sets or thermostatic valve trims.

Common questions

What is a rough-in shower valve?

It is the valve body that is plumbed into the wall before the tile goes up. The handle and escutcheon (the trim) are bought separately and mount over it.

Pressure-balance or thermostatic: which do I need?

Pressure-balance valves keep the hot and cold mix steady when pressure changes. Thermostatic valves hold a set temperature and are the usual choice for showers with several outlets.

Which connection type should I choose?

Pick the inlet that matches your supply pipe: sweat (CC) for copper, IPS for threaded pipe, or crimp ring or cold-expansion PEX. Many Moen M-PACT and M-CORE valves are listed by connection type in the title.

Common questions

Which Moen valve do I have?

Remove the handle and identify the cartridge, or check the installation paperwork. Posi-Temp, M-CORE and Moentrol valves each take their own cartridge and their own trim, so choose trim made for that valve family.

Is the valve included with Moen trim kits?

Usually not. Moen trim kits are the visible parts: handle, escutcheon and, where listed, the showerhead and tub spout. The rough-in valve is usually sold separately; check the listing, since the title says when a valve is included.

What does Posi-Temp mean?

Posi-Temp is Moen's pressure-balancing valve. It keeps the hot and cold mix steady when water pressure changes elsewhere in the house, such as when a toilet flushes.

Common questions

How do I find American Standard toilet parts for my toilet?

Look for the model number stamped inside the tank, usually on the back wall above the water line. Flappers, flush valves and tank-to-bowl kits are matched to the model. See toilet repair parts.

Which flapper fits my American Standard toilet?

Which cartridge fits my American Standard shower valve?

Ball valves are quarter-turn shut-off valves: a bored ball turns 90 degrees between fully open and fully closed. This collection covers ball valves for potable water, hydronic heating, steam, gas and compressed air, from 1/4" through 4".

Connections include FIP x FIP, sweat x sweat, press x press, flanged, and the PEX standards ASTM F1960 (cold expansion) and F1807 (crimp), so the valve can be joined the same way as the run it sits in. Bodies are brass, bronze, lead-free forged brass, no-lead dezincification resistant (DZR) brass, PVC and CPVC.

Pressure ratings on the product titles run from 125 psi on gas press valves to 600 WOG on threaded and sweat brass valves. Brands include Apollo-Conbraco, Jomar, Legend Valve, Milwaukee Valve, Red-White Valve, Viega and Webstone, including Webstone valves with hose drains and purge ports for hydronic service.

How to choose

  • End connection: match the joining method of the pipe: FIP thread, sweat (solder), press, F1960 expansion PEX, F1807 crimp PEX or solvent weld for PVC and CPVC.
  • Port: a full port valve passes the same bore as the pipe and is the one to use where pressure drop matters or the line will be rodded. A standard port valve has a smaller bore and suits isolation duty.
  • Lead-free status: anything installed on potable water must be lead-free, which is a legal requirement rather than a preference. Look for NL, LF or lead-free in the product title and the NSF/ANSI 372 marking on the valve.
  • Pressure rating: read the dual marking. A valve stamped 150 SWP / 600 WOG is rated 600 psi for water, oil and gas at ambient temperature but only 150 psi on saturated steam.
  • Body and trim: choose brass, bronze or DZR brass for the water quality, and a stainless steel ball and stem where the product offers one. Valves with a drain port let you empty the downstream side for service.

Common questions

What is the difference between a full port and a standard port ball valve?

A full port ball valve has a ball bored to the same diameter as the pipe, so it adds very little restriction. A standard port valve has a smaller bore, which restricts flow at the valve. Use full port on mains and wherever flow matters; standard port is acceptable for isolating a branch or a fixture.

What does 600 WOG mean on a ball valve?

WOG stands for water, oil, gas. It is the maximum non-shock working pressure in psi at ambient temperature, so 600 WOG means 600 psi. It is not the steam rating: steam pressure is marked separately as SWP or WSP and is much lower, for example 150 SWP.

Can I use a water ball valve on a gas line?

Only if the valve is listed for fuel gas. A brass ball valve sold for water is not automatically approved for gas service. Use a valve made and marked for gas, such as the ones in gas shut-off valves, and follow the gas code that applies where you are.

Shop by connection: FIP ball valves, sweat ball valves, press ball valves, PEX valves and plastic ball valves. For fuel gas, see gas shut-off valves.

Body HTML:
Press ball valves have press ends, so the valve goes into the line the same way the fittings do: no solder, no thread, no draining the system dry. Sizes run 1/2" through 4" in brass, lead-free brass and bronze, with press x press and press x hose connections.

The range includes Viega ProPress bronze valves rated 250 psi CWP, Viega MegaPress 316 stainless steel three-piece valves, Viega MegaPressG bronze valves for fuel gas piping, rated 125 psi with a locking handle, Jomar full port valves in dezincification resistant brass (250 WOG through 2", Press XLC at 200 WOG from 2-1/2" to 4"), Milwaukee Valve UPBA-480B low lead bronze valves, Apollo 77VLF lead-free brass valves, Webstone lead-free full port valves, Legend Valve LegendPress no-lead forged brass valves and Red-White Valve EzPress bronze valves.

How to choose

  • Press system: the press profile must match your jaws and your pipe, exactly as it does on the fittings. ProPress-style valves are for copper tube; Viega MegaPress valves are for the MegaPress steel pipe system.
  • Service: not every valve here is for water. Viega MegaPressG valves are made for fuel gas piping. Use a valve whose listing covers the fluid in the line.
  • Size: match the valve to the pipe size. Larger valves, such as Jomar Press XLC in 2-1/2" to 4", need the rings or jaws made for that size.
  • Lead-free status: on potable water the body must be lead-free. NSF/ANSI 372 compliance is a marking on the valve, not an assumption you can make from the alloy name.
  • Port: full port keeps the bore of the pipe. Standard port restricts flow at the valve, which is fine on isolation duty and a problem on a main.
  • Pressure rating: ratings here are 125 psi, 200 WOG or 250 WOG (CWP) depending on body and size. Check the figure in the product title against the system.

Specifying a system? Our press fitting technical specifications cover seal compounds, governing standards, jaw compatibility and installation steps.

Common questions

Do press ball valves work with any press tool?

No. The jaw or ring has to match the press profile and the size of the valve end. Check the valve manufacturer's list of approved tools and jaws before pressing, the same way you would for a fitting.

Are press ball valves approved for potable water?

The ones marked lead-free, low lead or no lead (NL, LF) in the product title are made for potable water. Confirm the NSF/ANSI 372 marking on the valve itself. Valves without that marking are for hydronic, gas or other non-potable service.

Can I use a press ball valve on PEX?

Not the valves in this collection: their press ends are made for metal pipe. For PEX, use a valve with F1960 expansion or F1807 crimp ends from our PEX valves.

Metafield: description_tag [string]: Press ball valves 1/2" to 4" in lead-free brass and bronze from Viega, Jomar, Milwaukee Valve, Apollo, Webstone and Legend. Match press system and port.

Body HTML:
Plastic ball valves from Legend Valve in PVC and CPVC. A plastic ball valve works the same way as a brass one, a quarter turn of the handle opens or closes it, but the body is made to be joined to plastic pipe.

The collection includes PVC compact-pattern ball valves with solvent x solvent ends and a tee handle from 1/2" to 2", PVC compact-pattern valves with FIP x FIP threaded ends from 1/2" to 1-1/2", and Schedule 80 gray CPVC compact-pattern valves with solvent ends and a tee handle from 1/2" to 2", with a full port ball design in 1/2", 3/4" and 1". It also holds Mini-Loc 1/4" and 3/8" push x push straight ball valves for small tubing.

How to choose

  • Material: PVC is the choice for cold water, irrigation and pool lines. CPVC is made for higher temperatures. Check the pressure and temperature rating of the valve either way.
  • End connection: solvent x solvent (socket) ends are cemented to the pipe; FIP x FIP ends thread onto male adapters. Mini-Loc valves push onto 1/4" or 3/8" tubing.
  • Size and schedule: match the nominal pipe size. The CPVC valves are Schedule 80 gray; use fittings and cement made for the same material.
  • Port: the 1/2", 3/4" and 1" CPVC valves are listed with a full port ball design. Confirm the port on other sizes if flow matters.

Common questions

What is the difference between a PVC and a CPVC ball valve?

Both are plastic quarter-turn valves, but they are different materials and are not cemented with the same products. PVC is used on cold water, irrigation and pool piping. CPVC handles higher temperatures. Match the valve to the pipe material and use the primer and cement made for it.

Can I use a PVC ball valve on hot water?

PVC is a cold water material. For higher temperature lines choose a CPVC valve and check the temperature rating published by Legend Valve for the model.

How do I seal a threaded plastic ball valve?

Use PTFE tape or a thread sealant rated for plastic, and do not overtighten: plastic female threads can crack. Solvent-weld valves need the correct primer and cement instead of tape.

Metafield: description_tag [string]: Legend Valve plastic ball valves: PVC compact valves with solvent-weld or FIP ends, Schedule 80 gray CPVC valves, 1/2" to 2", plus Mini-Loc push valves.

Body HTML:
Mini ball valves are small quarter-turn shut-off valves for instrument, gauge and low-flow lines, where a full size valve does not fit. This collection holds Legend Valve forged brass mini ball valves with a large port and a transition pattern: male pipe thread (MNPT) on one end and female pipe thread (FNPT) on the other, so the valve threads straight into a port and accepts a fitting or gauge on the outlet.

Four models are listed: 101-520 in 1/8" and 101-521 in 1/4" with a lever handle, and 101-530 in 1/8" and 101-531 in 1/4" with a tee handle. Typical uses are gauge isolation, air lines, drain points and equipment connections.

How to choose

  • Size: 1/8" or 1/4" nominal pipe thread. Measure the port you are threading into, not the tubing.
  • End connection: all four are MIP x FIP. Confirm which side of your connection is male and which is female.
  • Handle: a lever handle is easier to grip; a tee handle needs less swing room and suits tight spaces.
  • Rating and service: check the pressure and temperature rating for the service. These models are not listed as no-lead in their titles, so confirm suitability before using one on potable water.

Common questions

What is a mini ball valve used for?

To shut off a small line: isolating a pressure gauge, an air line, a drain or sample point, or a connection to a piece of equipment. It works like any ball valve, with a quarter turn from open to closed.

What does MIP x FIP mean?

MIP is male iron pipe thread and FIP is female iron pipe thread, the same threads as MNPT and FNPT. A MIP x FIP valve has one male end and one female end, so it can go directly into a female port without a nipple.

Do you have mini valves for 1/4" or 3/8" tubing?

Yes. Legend Valve Mini-Loc push x push straight ball valves in 1/4" and 3/8" are listed with our plastic ball valves.

Related: ball valves, FIP ball valves, Legend Valve, pressure gauges and brass fittings.

Metafield: description_tag [string]: Legend Valve forged brass mini ball valves in 1/8" and 1/4" MIP x FIP, with lever or tee handle, for gauges, air lines, drain points and equipment.

Body HTML:
Gas shut-off valves, also called gas cocks or gas ball valves, isolate an appliance or a branch of gas piping with a quarter turn. This collection holds threaded gas ball valves from Jomar and Legend Valve.

Jomar two-piece FIP gas ball valves come in 1/2" (102-603), 3/4" (102-604) and 1" (102-605), rated 175 WOG, plus a 1/2" two-piece valve rated 400 WOG (102-503). Legend Valve Blue Top valves are one-piece forged brass gas ball valves with FNPT x FNPT ends in 1/2" (102-103) and 3/4" (102-104).

Use a valve listed for fuel gas service and for the pressure in your system, and install an accessible shutoff at each appliance as the code requires. Match the thread size to the gas line, apply a gas-rated thread sealant, and leak test every joint after installation.

How to choose

  • Size: 1/2", 3/4" or 1" FIP, matched to the gas pipe or the appliance connection.
  • Listing: the valve must be made and marked for fuel gas. Check the listing shown on the valve and the manufacturer sheet against what your inspector accepts.
  • Pressure rating: 175 WOG on the Jomar 102-603, 102-604 and 102-605; 400 WOG on the Jomar 102-503. Confirm the gas pressure rating on the valve tag.
  • Body style: one-piece forged brass (Legend Valve Blue Top) or two-piece (Jomar). Both are quarter-turn.

Common questions

What is the difference between a gas cock and a gas ball valve?

In current use the terms mean the same thing: a manual quarter-turn shutoff on a gas line. Older gas cocks were plug valves; the valves here are ball valves made for gas service.

Can I use a regular water ball valve as a gas shut-off?

No, unless it is also listed for fuel gas. A gas shut-off has to carry a gas listing accepted by the code in force. The valves in this collection are sold as gas ball valves.

Where does a gas shut-off valve go?

Codes require an accessible shutoff valve at each gas appliance, ahead of the flexible connector, in addition to the main shutoff at the meter. Work on gas piping should be done by a qualified person and leak tested.

Related: gas valves for furnaces and boilers, gas supply, flexible gas pipe and press ball valves.

Point-of-use mixing valves are thermostatic valves installed at a single fixture, usually under a sink or at a tub, to limit the temperature of the water that reaches the outlet. They blend hot and cold supply water to a set point, which is the anti-scald protection that plumbing codes commonly call for at public lavatories.

The collection includes the Caleffi SinkMixer in 3/8" compression (ASSE 1070, lead free), the Caleffi TubMixer in 3/8" compression, 1/2" and 3/4" NPT, 3/4" sweat and 3/4" PEX expansion (ASSE 1070), Cash Acme HG135 series 3/8" lead free valves, the Resideo UMV500-LF 3/8" universal undersink valve for 3 or 4 port setups, and the Watts LFUSG-B 3/8" lead free valve, adjustable from 80 to 120 F.

How to choose

  • Standard: check the certification the code calls for at the fixture, commonly ASSE 1070 for water temperature limiting devices. It is stated in the title of the Caleffi models; confirm it on the manufacturer sheet for the others.
  • Connection: 3/8" compression fits between the angle stops and the faucet supply lines. Tub models come in 1/2" and 3/4" NPT, sweat or PEX expansion.
  • Temperature range: confirm the adjustable outlet range, for example 80 to 120 F on the Watts LFUSG-B.
  • Lead-free status: these valves carry potable water, so choose a lead free (LF) model.
  • Space and ports: check the room under the sink, whether check valves are built in, and whether you need a 3 port or 4 port arrangement.

Common questions

What is a point-of-use mixing valve?

It is a small thermostatic mixing valve installed at one fixture. It mixes hot and cold water to a safe outlet temperature and holds it there, so the water heater can be kept hot while the faucet or tub delivers tempered water.

What is ASSE 1070?

ASSE 1070 is the performance standard for water temperature limiting devices, the valves used at individual fixtures such as lavatories and tubs. A valve at the water heater that tempers the whole distribution system is covered by a different standard, ASSE 1017.

Where is an under-sink mixing valve installed?

Between the hot and cold stops and the faucet, inside the cabinet. The hot and cold supplies connect to the valve inlets and the mixed outlet feeds the hot side of the faucet. Follow the installation sheet for the model.

Related: all mixing valves, thermostatic mixing valves, high flow mixing valves, angle stops and supply lines.

An automatic water heater shut-off valve sits on the cold water supply to the heater and closes it when a sensor finds water on the floor or in the drain pan. The heater is often installed where nobody looks, so a leak can run for a long time before it is noticed; the valve stops the supply from feeding it.

The kits in this collection are all 3/4" NPT. The Taco LeakBreaker (LB-075-H-2LF) is a control unit, a valve with actuator and a water sensor, made for a water heater. The LeakBreaker eLink adds WiFi and reports status and changes. The FloodStop 20001 water heater kit has a 3/4" NPT MIP x FIP valve with a control unit and a sensor.

A shut-off on the heater protects the heater only. To cover the whole house, use a valve on the main line from water leak detectors and smart shut-off valves.

How to choose

  • Size and end connection: all the kits here are 3/4" NPT. The FloodStop 20001 valve is MIP x FIP; the Taco LB-075-H-2LF valve is listed as male thread on both ends. Check the thread gender against the nipple and connector on your heater.
  • Local alarm or WiFi: the LeakBreaker signals with a two-color LED and an audible alarm at the control unit. The eLink version also sends status and change notifications over WiFi, which matters when nobody is near the heater to hear the alarm.
  • Sensor position: the sensor goes at the low point of the drain pan or on the floor beside the heater. Confirm on the manufacturer sheet how many sensors the kit includes and whether more can be added.
  • Lead-free status: the valve is on a potable water line, so it must be lead-free. The Taco part numbers here end in LF; confirm the marking on the valve.
  • Power: the control unit needs power at the heater. Check the supply the kit requires on the manufacturer sheet before installation.

Common questions

Where is a water heater shut-off valve installed?

On the cold water inlet, upstream of the heater, with the sensor at the low point of the drain pan or on the floor. When the sensor detects water, the control closes the valve and the supply to the heater stops.

Does a water heater shut-off valve protect the whole house?

No. It closes the supply to the water heater only. Leaks elsewhere need a point sensor or a whole-house valve on the main, such as the ones in Flo by Moen.

Can the valve be reset after it closes?

The Taco LeakBreaker is resettable and testable after a trip. Find and repair the leak, dry the sensor, then reset the control following the manufacturer instructions.

Related: water leak detectors and shut-off valves, FloodStop appliance kits, Flo by Moen, water heater pans and water heaters.

Water pressure regulators, also called pressure reducing valves or PRVs, sit on the incoming water service and hold downstream pressure at a set point. The trade calls the device a PRV and the fixture aisle calls it a water pressure regulator; they are the same valve.

This collection covers regulators and service parts from 1/2" through 2": Resideo DS05 and DS06 DialSet, Watts 009 series, Cash Acme EB45, Zurn Wilkins 600XL, 70XL and NR3XL, and Caleffi PressCal. Ends cover female NPT, solder union, press, PEX-A cold expansion and push-to-connect. The Resideo DS05, the DS06 DialSet and the Cash Acme EB45 each come in several end configurations of one valve body, so choose the body for the pressure job and the ends for the pipe you are joining.

How to choose

  • Size: match the service line, 1/2" through 2".
  • End connection: female NPT, solder (sweat) union, press, PEX-A cold expansion or push-to-connect. The connection is a separate choice from the valve.
  • Adjustment range: the standard range is 25 to 75 psi and covers nearly every residential service. Low range valves adjust 10 to 35 psi. Winding a 25 to 75 psi valve down to its bottom stop is not the same as fitting a low range valve.
  • Single or double union: a single union valve is solid on one end, so replacing it later means cutting pipe. A double union breaks loose at both ends.
  • Standard and lead-free status: regulators on potable water must be lead-free. The Caleffi PressCal valves are listed to ASSE 1003, the standard for water pressure reducing valves.

What to know before installing a regulator

A pressure reducing valve and a pressure relief valve do opposite jobs. A regulator holds downstream pressure at a set point continuously, whether or not anything is wrong. A relief valve does nothing at all until pressure or temperature crosses a limit, then opens and discharges. One is a control, the other is a safety device, and neither substitutes for the other.

Installing a regulator closes the system, and a closed system needs somewhere for hot water to expand. Before the regulator, thermal expansion from the water heater pushed back out into the street main. After it, the regulator blocks that path, pressure climbs every time the heater fires, and the T&P valve on the heater begins to weep. The answer is a correctly sized thermal expansion tank put in at the same time, not a second T&P valve.

Seats and gauges. Where Watts states the seat, it tracks size: polymer seat in 1/2" through 1", stainless steel seat in 1-1/4" through 2". Caleffi PressCal valves come in female NPT, press and union sweat, most with an integral pressure gauge.

Rebuild before replacing. Service parts are listed here alongside the valves: Resideo union kits, union nuts, tailpieces and gaskets, a low lead replacement filter bowl with O-ring for the 1-1/2" and 2" DS06, and valve inserts. A regulator that will not hold its setting is often a fouled strainer or a cut seal rather than a failed body; the DS06 carries its strainer in a replaceable bowl for that reason.

Common questions

When do I need a water pressure regulator?

Most plumbing codes call for a regulator wherever static supply pressure at the building exceeds 80 psi. Measure the street pressure with a gauge before choosing a set point rather than working from the reputation of the neighborhood.

Is a PRV the same as a water pressure regulator?

Yes. Pressure reducing valve, PRV and water pressure regulator are names for the same device. It is not the same as a pressure relief valve, which is a safety device that only opens when a limit is exceeded.

Why does my water heater relief valve drip after a regulator was installed?

The regulator closes the system, so heated water has nowhere to expand and pressure rises until the T&P valve weeps. That usually points to a missing or failed thermal expansion tank, not to a failed T&P valve.

Related: backflow preventers, check valves, relief valves, expansion tanks and pressure gauges. Regulators are also covered in our valve reference guide.

Backflow preventers keep water that has left the potable system from flowing back into it. This collection covers backflow prevention devices from Watts, Zurn Wilkins, Apollo-Conbraco, Arrowhead Brass, Caleffi, Cash Acme, Resideo and Moen. Assemblies run 1/4" through 3", and most of the range is lead free bronze or lead free brass.

The range breaks down as reduced pressure principle (RP) and reduced pressure zone (RPZ) assemblies, double check valve assemblies, dual check valves, hose connection vacuum breakers, atmospheric and anti-siphon vacuum breakers, a pressure vacuum breaker, air gap fittings, and Zurn Wilkins repair kits and internals for the 375, 375XL, 950XL, 975XL and 975XL2.

The device class is set by the hazard, not by the pipe size, and the local code or water purveyor decides which class a connection needs.

How to choose

  • Device class: a reduced pressure assembly (RP or RPZ) is what a high hazard connection needs. A double check assembly is a low hazard device. A pressure vacuum breaker (PVB) protects against back-siphonage only, not back-pressure.
  • Standard: ASSE 1013 covers reduced pressure principle assemblies and ASSE 1015 covers double checks; the number on the tag is what the inspector reads.
  • Size and end connection: 1/4" through 3". Match the line size; do not size the device down to fit a budget.
  • Testable or not: reduced pressure and double check assemblies carry test cocks and in most jurisdictions have to be certified by a licensed tester at installation and then annually.
  • Pressure and temperature: where the manufacturer publishes limits, the devices are rated 175 psi maximum working pressure and 180 F maximum temperature.

Which backflow preventer goes where

A reduced pressure assembly has a relief port that dumps to atmosphere the moment either check fouls, so a failure is visible on the floor instead of silent in the potable line. A double check assembly fails closed without telling anyone. Substituting down a class is the one substitution that is never a field call.

On a lawn irrigation or sprinkler system the local code decides between a PVB and an RPZ backflow preventer, and the answer usually turns on whether fertilizer or chemical is injected downstream. A hose bib backflow preventer, a hose connection vacuum breaker threaded onto the sillcock, is the protection most often missing. A residential service entrance is typically a dual check, listed from 1/4" through 1".

Rebuilding is often an alternative to replacing. Zurn Wilkins repair kits cover the 375, 375XL, 950XL, 975XL and 975XL2 from 1/4" through 2": rubber and spring kits for an annual test failure, complete internals when the seats are cut. Match the kit to the model number on the tag, not to the pipe size.

Common questions

What is the difference between an RPZ and a double check backflow preventer?

Both have two check valves in series. A reduced pressure zone assembly adds a relief valve between them that opens to atmosphere if a check leaks, so it is accepted on high hazard connections. A double check assembly has no relief port and is a low hazard device.

Do backflow preventers need to be tested?

Testable assemblies, meaning reduced pressure and double check assemblies with test cocks, have to be certified by a licensed tester at installation and then annually in most jurisdictions. That obligation follows the building, so check what your water purveyor requires.

What backflow preventer do I need for a sprinkler system?

The local code decides. Irrigation systems commonly use a pressure vacuum breaker or a reduced pressure assembly, and the choice usually depends on whether fertilizer or chemicals are injected downstream. Ask the local authority before buying.

Related: check valves, pressure reducing valves, mixing valves, sillcocks and Zurn Wilkins. Backflow devices are also covered in our valve reference guide.

Check valves let flow pass in one direction and close against flow in the other. This collection covers swing, spring and in-line check valves for potable water, hydronic heating and pump discharge, in 1/2" through 2" and larger.

Orientation is the specification people get wrong. A swing check relies on gravity and flow to close its disc, so it only works reliably in a horizontal run or a vertical run with upward flow. A spring check closes against a spring and works in any orientation, which is why it is the right choice on pump discharge and in tight mechanical rooms.

Bodies are bronze, brass, lead-free brass and cast iron, with FIP, sweat, press and F1960 expansion ends, plus cast iron wafer and flanged valves. Brands include Jomar, Milwaukee Valve, Legend Valve, Red-White Valve, Apollo-Conbraco and Viega.

How to choose

  • Type: swing check for horizontal runs and low pressure drop; spring or in-line check for vertical runs, pump discharge and any orientation.
  • Size and end connection: match the pipe size and joining method: FIP, sweat, press, F1960 expansion, wafer or flange.
  • Pressure drop: spring checks have a higher cracking pressure and a higher pressure drop. On a gravity or low-head system that difference matters; on a pumped line it usually does not.
  • Material and lead-free status: use a lead-free or no-lead valve on potable water. Bronze and cast iron valves without that marking are for hydronic and mechanical piping.
  • Pressure rating: ratings in the product titles run from 200 WOG to 600 WOG, with Class 125 for cast iron. Check the figure for the model.

Common questions

Can a swing check valve be installed vertically?

Only with flow going up. A swing check needs gravity and reverse flow to close its disc, so it will not seat on a downflow line or if it is installed backwards. For any other position use a spring or in-line check valve.

What is the difference between a swing check and a spring check valve?

A swing check has a hinged disc that the flow pushes open; it offers little resistance but depends on orientation. A spring check has a disc or poppet held closed by a spring; it works in any position, at the cost of a higher pressure drop.

Which way does a check valve go?

Follow the arrow cast or stamped on the body: it points in the direction of flow. On a pump, the check valve goes on the discharge side with the arrow pointing away from the pump.

Related: backflow preventers, ball valves, gate valves, sump and sewage check valves and backwater valves.

Shower and tub diverter valves, in-wall rough-in bodies and transfer valves, mostly with 1/2" inlets. A diverter sends water from the mixing valve to one outlet or another: tub spout to showerhead, or between several shower outlets. The mixing valve sets the temperature; the diverter only chooses where the water goes.

A transfer valve is the related but different device: it can feed two outlets at once, which is what a body spray and rain head combination needs. Choosing a diverter where a transfer valve was intended means only one outlet ever runs.

Brands include Moen (M-CORE transfer valves and Posi-Temp with diverter), Grohe, hansgrohe, Delta, Brizo, American Standard, Pfister, TOTO and DXV, with 2-way, 3-way and 3-or-6-function diverter and transfer valve roughs.

How to choose

  • Brand and family: start with the brand and family of your mixing valve and trim. Trim is not cross-compatible between brands or between generations.
  • Number of outlets: count outlets before ordering. A 2-way diverter switches between two outlets; a 3-way handles three. The number is fixed by the valve body in the wall, not by the trim.
  • Shared or discrete functions: a diverter with shared positions, or a transfer valve, can run two outlets together. A discrete diverter runs one at a time.
  • Inlet connection and size: sweat, IPS (threaded) or PEX, 1/2" on most models here and 3/4" on some hansgrohe roughs.
  • Rough-in and trim: on most systems the rough-in body and the finish trim are ordered separately, so the valve goes in during construction and the finish is chosen at the end.

Popular in this collection: Pfister 015-6WDS 4-Port 6-Way Diverter Valve, American Standard Flash 2-Way/3-Way Shared Diverter, Moen U362CIS M-CORE Mixing Valve with Transfer Valve, Moen U361CI M-CORE Transfer Valve.

Common questions

What does a shower diverter valve do?

A shower diverter valve sends water from the mixing valve to one outlet or another, such as the showerhead, a hand shower or a tub spout. The mixing valve sets the temperature; the diverter only chooses where the water goes.

Diverter valve vs transfer valve: what is the difference?

A diverter valve sends all the water to one outlet at a time, such as the tub spout or the showerhead. A transfer valve can also run two outlets together, for example a rain head and body sprays. If you want two outlets on at the same time, choose a transfer valve or a diverter with shared positions.

Can I use a different brand of trim on my diverter valve?

No. The trim has to be made for the rough-in valve in the wall, so match the brand and model of the valve body. The rough-in and the trim are sold separately, and adding an outlet later means opening the wall.

Related: shower and tub-shower valves, diverter valve trims, shower trim sets, thermostatic valve trims and Moen.

Body HTML:
Angle stops and straight stops are the small shut-off valves under every sink and toilet. This collection covers supply stops from BrassCraft, Legend Valve, Dahl Valve, LSP Products, Grohe and BK Products, in angle, straight and dual-outlet bodies, plus tees, kits and service stops.

Nearly every one of these ends in 3/8" or 1/4" compression on the fixture side, because that is what a supply line expects. The inlet is where the choice lives, and it has to match the pipe already in the wall: compression for copper stub-outs, FIP, F1960 expansion PEX, F1807 crimp PEX, push-fit, press or CPVC.

How to choose

  • Angle or straight: an angle stop turns the flow 90 degrees, for a supply pipe that comes out of the wall. A straight stop passes flow in line, for a pipe that comes up out of the floor. Look at the stub-out before you buy, not at the fixture.
  • Inlet connection: compression for copper stub-outs; FIP threaded onto a male adapter or nipple; F1960 expansion for PEX-a; F1807 crimp; push-fit; press; or CPVC solvent weld.
  • Size: the inlet is usually 1/2" nominal (5/8" OD compression on copper). The outlet is 3/8" OD compression for most faucets and toilets, or 1/4" for ice makers and similar lines.
  • Quarter-turn or multi-turn: a quarter-turn stop is a ball valve with PTFE seats. A multi-turn stop is a compression washer on a rising stem.
  • Lead-free status: on a potable line the stop has to be certified lead-free: a weighted average of no more than 0.25 percent lead on wetted surfaces, certified to NSF/ANSI 372.

Quarter-turn versus multi-turn

A quarter-turn stop is a ball valve: a chrome ball with a hole through it, sealed by two PTFE seats. A multi-turn stop is a compression washer on a rising stem. The difference matters after ten years, not on day one: the multi-turn washer hardens, bonds to the seat, and can shear off when someone finally tries to close it during a leak. That is why a plumber replacing a faucet replaces the stop too. The Legend 114-201NL is the one deliberate multi-turn in the range.

A compression ferrule is single-use

The brass ring that seals a compression inlet deforms permanently when you tighten the nut. It has taken the shape of that pipe at that depth. Pull the valve off and reuse the old ferrule and it will weep. Cut the stub back and start with a new ferrule, or use a push-fit or press inlet where the seal is a captured O-ring rather than a crushed ring.

Push-fit and press inlets

Push-fit stops, including Legend Insta-Loc II (114-903NL, 114-904NL, 114-943NL) and the BrassCraft G2PS and G2QPS series, go on a clean cut stub with no tool at all. LegendPress stops (114-903PNL, 114-904PNL, 114-913PNL) take a standard press jaw; see press tools and jaws. Both are useful in a cabinet you cannot get two wrenches into. If you are on PEX, the inlet has to match your system: see F1960 expansion fittings and F1807 crimp fittings.

Dual stops, tees and loose key stops

Dual-outlet stops and tees let one stub-out feed two things: a toilet plus a bidet seat, a sink plus a reverse-osmosis unit, a dishwasher teed off the hot side. The BrassCraft CR1900DVX and R1700DVX families and Legend 114-801NL and 114-802NL give two independently controlled outlets, usually 3/8" and 1/4". The BrassCraft CT2-664X P and BK 993-016NL are plain tees with no second valve, so you cannot shut one branch without the other.

The BrassCraft KTSCR19X and SCR19X have no handle. They take a removable key, which is what you want in a rental, a school restroom or anywhere a handle would get turned by someone who should not be turning it. Order the key separately.

Common questions

What is the difference between an angle stop and a straight stop?

An angle stop turns the flow 90 degrees and is used when the supply pipe comes out of the wall. A straight stop passes flow in line and is used when the pipe comes up through the floor. The valve is otherwise identical inside.

What size angle stop do I need?

Check the inlet first: a 1/2" copper stub-out takes a 5/8" OD compression inlet, usually listed as 1/2" nominal; threaded and PEX inlets are listed by pipe size. The outlet is 3/8" OD compression for most faucet and toilet supply lines and 1/4" for ice makers.

Can I reuse the old compression nut and ferrule?

It is not recommended. The ferrule deforms to fit the pipe the first time it is tightened and tends to weep if reused with a new valve. Cut the stub back and use the new ferrule supplied with the stop, or choose a push-fit or press inlet.

Related: supply lines, angle stops only, stops and risers, toilet repair parts and BrassCraft.

Body HTML:
Water leak detectors and smart water shut-off valves for domestic water: whole-house motorized ball valves, appliance-specific shut-off kits, and WiFi point sensors that also watch for freezing. Brands are Moen, First Alert, Resideo, Taco Comfort Solutions and FloodStop.

There are three kinds of device here. A whole-house valve goes on the main and closes the entire supply when a leak is detected. An appliance shut-off kit protects one known failure point, such as a water heater or washing machine. A point sensor raises the alarm but closes nothing. Not sure which you need? Our whole-house water leak detection guide covers valve sizing, where each device installs and how the sensors are wired.

How to choose

  • Whole house or one appliance: a whole-house valve installs on the main downstream of the service shutoff. An appliance kit covers a single point: water heater, washing machine, ice maker, toilet or dishwasher.
  • Valve size: size the valve to the line you are cutting into, not to a fixture branch. The First Alert L5 comes in 1/2", 3/4", 1" and 1-1/4" NPT; Flo by Moen in 3/4", 1" and 1-1/4".
  • End connection: NPT on the whole-house valves; FloodStop kits use 3/4" NPT MIP x FIP for a water heater, two 3/4" 90-degree valves for a washing machine, 1/4" compression for an ice maker and 3/8" compression for a toilet or dishwasher.
  • Alerts: WiFi models send notifications to a phone app. Devices without WiFi sound a local alarm only.
  • Sensors: check how many sensors or how much sensing cable the device supports for the area you need to cover.

The three device types

Whole-house shut-off valves. The First Alert L5 is a WiFi actuator on a ball valve, in 1/2", 3/4", 1" and 1-1/4" NPT. Some kits are listed with a leak sensor and some without, so check what the product page includes. Flo by Moen puts detection and shut-off in one body, in 3/4", 1" and 1-1/4". A 1" main needs a 1" valve or the whole house loses pressure through the device.

Appliance shut-off kits. FloodStop builds one kit per appliance. The Taco LeakBreaker is water-heater specific: a control unit with valve, actuator and sensor that shuts the supply to the heater, with a two-color LED and an audible alarm. It is re-settable and testable after a trip, and the eLink version reports status over WiFi.

Point sensors. The First Alert L1 detects water on its own base or anywhere along its 5 ft sensing cable, runs on WiFi with no hub, sounds a 100 dB alarm and sends an app notification. It also reads temperature and humidity, so it can warn before a pipe freezes. Battery life runs up to three years, the unit is reusable once wiped dry, and cables daisy-chain to cover up to 500 feet from a single detector.

Popular in this collection: Resideo CHW3610W1001/U Water Leak Detector with Cable Sensor, First Alert VWS02Y-1 L5 WiFi Actuator with 1 in NPT Ball Valve.

Common questions

Whole-house shut-off or appliance shut-off?

A whole-house valve installs on the main water line and can shut off the entire home when a leak is detected. An appliance shut-off protects one point, such as a water heater, washing machine or ice maker.

Do water leak detectors need Wi-Fi?

Wi-Fi models send alerts to your phone and can close a valve remotely. Battery-only detectors sound a local alarm, which helps only if someone is home to hear it.

What size shut-off valve do I need?

Match the size of the main water line where the valve will be installed. Valves are offered from 1/2 in to 1-1/4 in NPT.

Related: Flo by Moen, water heater shut-off valves, sump pumps, relief valves and ball valves.

Body HTML:
Flo by Moen, often searched as Moen Flo, puts leak detection and automatic shut-off in one body plumbed into the main, plus battery puck detectors for the fixtures the main valve cannot see.

Smart Water Shutoff valves install in line on the main water supply, downstream of the service shutoff. The unit monitors flow, pressure and temperature, runs a pressure test on the plumbing, and closes the supply on its own when it reads a leak. It is WiFi enabled and reports to a phone app. Available in 0.75 in. (900-001), 1 in. (900-006) and 1.25 in. (900-002).

Smart Water Detectors are battery pucks that watch one spot and report to the same app as the valve. They sense water, temperature and humidity. Sold singly (920-004) or in a three-pack (920-005).

How to choose

  • Valve size: size the valve to the pipe you are cutting into, not to a fixture branch. A 1 in. main needs the 1 in. unit or the whole house loses pressure through the device.
  • Location: the shutoff needs a spot on the main after the service shutoff, within reach of a power outlet and WiFi. The 25 ft extension cable (920-003) reaches an outlet further away than the stock lead allows.
  • Detectors: put one at each risk point: a water heater pan, under a sink base, behind a laundry box or at a sump. The three-pack suits a house with several.
  • Sensing cable: the 6 ft Smart Leak Detect sensing cable (920-006) extends a puck along a run of pipe or the length of a pan, where a single point would miss the water.

Pairing note: the shutoff valve and the detectors work independently, but on the same account the detectors can trigger the valve to close. A whole-house valve without detectors still catches a leak downstream of itself by flow signature; detectors without a valve raise the alarm but close nothing. A Flo by Moen service kit (935-001) is also listed.

Common questions

What size Moen Flo do I need?

Choose the size of your main water line: 3/4 in. (900-001), 1 in. (900-006) or 1-1/4 in. (900-002). Do not size it to a fixture branch, because all the water in the house passes through the device.

Where is the Flo by Moen Smart Water Shutoff installed?

In line on the main water supply, downstream of the service shutoff, so that every fixture is behind it. It needs power and a WiFi connection. Follow the Moen installation instructions for the location and clearances.

Do I need the Smart Water Detectors if I have the shutoff valve?

They are optional. The valve detects leaks downstream of itself from flow, pressure and temperature. Detectors add coverage at specific spots and report temperature and humidity; on the same account they can trigger the valve to close.

Sewage pumps move wastewater with solids from a basin up to a gravity sewer or septic line, for a basement bathroom or any fixture below the sewer. This collection covers sewage ejector pumps, grinder pumps, packaged systems and their accessories from Liberty Pumps and Zoeller.

Liberty Pumps models include the LE41 (4/10 HP) and LE51 (1/2 HP) sewage pumps with 2" discharge, the 1 HP PRG101 with 2" discharge, and the 2 HP LSG202 and LSG203 grinder pumps with 1-1/4" discharge, along with simplex and duplex sewage packages. Zoeller models include the M267 automatic and N267 non-automatic 1/2 HP sewage ejector pumps with 2" NPT discharge, 912 simplex sewage packages and a 915 simplex grinder package with an 18" x 30" basin. Basins, access risers, float switches and high-water alarms are listed here too.

How to choose

  • Pump type: a sewage ejector pump passes solids to a gravity line; a grinder pump cuts solids and suits long runs or a pressure main.
  • Head and flow: size by total dynamic head and the flow you need, using the manufacturer pump curve.
  • Discharge size: 2" on the sewage pumps and the PRG101 here, 1-1/4" on the LSG grinder pumps and the Zoeller 915 grinder package.
  • Voltage and phase: 115 V single phase on most models; the 2 HP grinders are 208-230 V in single phase (LSG202) or three phase (LSG203).
  • Automatic or manual: automatic models have a float switch; manual or non-automatic models need a separate control. Check basin size, venting and check valve requirements, and fit a high-water alarm.

Common questions

What is the difference between a sewage pump and a grinder pump?

A sewage ejector pump passes solids whole and discharges to a gravity sewer or septic line. A grinder pump cuts solids into a slurry and can pump it through smaller pipe over a longer distance or into a pressure main.

What is the difference between a simplex and a duplex package?

A simplex package has one pump in the basin. A duplex package has two pumps that share the basin, so one can run if the other fails or is being serviced.

Do I need a high-water alarm?

An alarm tells you the water level in the basin is too high, which usually means the pump or its switch has failed. Fitting one lets a failed pump be noticed before a backup.

Jomar valves for water, gas and hydronic systems. The catalog here is mainly two-piece ball valves: full port valves in dezincification resistant brass with press, Press XLC, FIP threaded and sweat connections from 1/2" to 4", rated 600 WOG in threaded and sweat and 200 to 250 WOG in press; standard port PEX valves with F1960 expansion and F1807 crimp ends rated 400 WOG; valves with a drain or hose outlet; and gas ball valves in 1/2", 3/4" and 1" FIP.

Beyond ball valves, Jomar products include in-line and horizontal swing check valves, non-rising stem gate valves, TGG variable orifice balance valves in FIP and sweat from 1/2" to 2", lug style butterfly valves with an epoxy-coated ductile iron body and stainless steel disc, tankless water heater valve kits, stem extensions for insulated lines, and stainless steel sink strainers.

How to choose

  • End connection: match the pipe and joining method: press, Press XLC for 2-1/2" to 4", FIP, sweat, F1960 expansion or F1807 crimp.
  • Port: full port bodies reduce flow restriction through the valve; the PEX valves here are standard port.
  • Pressure rating: check the WOG figure in the title: 600 WOG on threaded and sweat ball valves, 250 WOG on press through 2", 200 WOG on Press XLC, 400 WOG on PEX valves, 175 WOG on most gas ball valves.
  • Material: many of the ball valves are listed in dezincification resistant brass. Confirm lead-free status on the product page before potable use.
  • Accessories: add a stem extension where pipe insulation would otherwise cover the handle.

Common questions

What is Jomar Press XLC?

Press XLC is the press connection used on the larger Jomar ball valves, 2-1/2" to 4", rated 200 WOG in the product titles. Sizes 1/2" to 2" use the standard press connection rated 250 WOG.

Does Jomar make gas ball valves?

Yes. Jomar two-piece FIP gas ball valves in 1/2", 3/4" and 1" are listed with our gas shut-off valves.

Legend Valve makes valves and fittings for plumbing and hydronic systems, and the range here is wide. Fittings make up most of it: no-lead brass threaded fittings and nipples, stainless steel fittings and nipples, PEX fittings in brass and composite, and Mini-Loc push fittings for small tubing.

Valves include no-lead forged brass full port ball valves with FIP, sweat and LegendPress ends, PEX ball valves with F1960 and F1807 ends, forged brass mini ball valves, Blue Top gas ball valves, PVC and CPVC compact ball valves, quarter-turn angle and straight supply stops (including Insta-Loc II push-fit and LegendPress), swing check valves, gate valves, and no-lead cast bronze Y-strainers with a 20-mesh stainless steel screen. Plate heat exchangers are listed too.

How to choose

  • Lead-free status: for potable water, confirm the part is marked no lead. Many Legend no-lead part numbers end in NL.
  • Size and thread: check the nominal pipe size and the thread gender (FIP or MIP), and whether you need a reducing fitting or a street pattern.
  • End connection: valves come with FIP, sweat, LegendPress, F1960, F1807, push-fit or solvent-weld ends. Match the joining method of the pipe.
  • Material: no-lead brass for general plumbing; stainless steel for corrosive or high-purity applications where brass is not suitable; PVC or CPVC for plastic piping.

Common questions

What does NL mean in a Legend Valve part number?

NL stands for no lead. Parts such as 101-004NL or 114-903NL are the no-lead versions intended for potable water. Parts without the suffix should be checked before use on drinking water.

What is LegendPress?

LegendPress is the Legend Valve line of press-connection valves, including ball valves, check valves and supply stops. The ends are pressed onto the tube with a press tool instead of being soldered or threaded.

Does Legend Valve make fittings as well as valves?

Yes. A large part of the Legend range here is fittings: no-lead brass and stainless steel threaded fittings and nipples, and PEX fittings.

Shopping for Milwaukee valves? This collection covers the Milwaukee Valve line we stock: bronze and brass ball valves with threaded, sweat and press ends, bronze gate, globe and check valves, and cast iron flanged gate, swing check, wafer check and lug butterfly valves for larger mechanical piping.

Milwaukee Valve is a valve manufacturer, not to be confused with Milwaukee Tool, the power tool brand. Milwaukee Valve makes bronze, brass and cast iron valves for plumbing, hydronic heating and mechanical piping systems.

Start with the end connection that matches your pipe, then confirm the WOG or SWP pressure rating on the product page.

How to choose

  • Valve type: ball valves for quarter-turn shutoff, gate valves for full-bore isolation, globe valves for throttling, check valves to stop reverse flow, butterfly valves for larger lines.
  • End connection: FIP, sweat, press or flange, matched to your piping.
  • Pressure rating: confirm the WOG (water, oil, gas) and SWP (steam) figures in the title, for example 150 SWP / 600 WOG on BA-100 bronze ball valves or 125 SWP / 200 WOG on cast iron flanged valves.
  • Material and lead content: bronze, brass or cast iron. For potable water choose a valve listed as low lead, such as the UPBA-480B press ball valves.
  • Port: full port or standard port on ball valves; the product title states which.

Milwaukee Valve series in this collection

  • Ball valves: BA-100, BA-400 and BA-475B threaded (FIP) valves, BA-150, BA-450 and BA-485B sweat valves, UPBA-480B and BA-480B press valves, and hose end versions.
  • Gate valves: 105, 1151 and 1182 bronze FIP gate valves and 2885-M flanged cast iron OS&Y gate valves.
  • Check valves: 507, 509 and 510 bronze swing checks, 548T and 1548T spring checks, 1509 and 1510 sweat checks, 2974-M flanged swing checks and 1403, 1404, 1406 and 1425 cast iron wafer checks.
  • Globe and butterfly valves: 502 and 590T bronze globe valves, BB2-100 bronze butterfly valves and CL223E lug style cast iron butterfly valves.

Our valve reference guide compares ball, gate, globe and check valves.

Common questions

Is Milwaukee Valve the same company as Milwaukee Tool?

No. Milwaukee Valve is a valve manufacturer; Milwaukee Tool is the power tool brand. They are separate companies. Milwaukee power tools are in our Milwaukee Tools collection.

What do WOG and SWP mean on a Milwaukee valve?

WOG is the non-shock pressure rating in psi for water, oil and gas at ambient temperature. SWP is the steam working pressure. A valve marked 150 SWP / 600 WOG is rated 600 psi on cold water and 150 psi on steam.

Which Milwaukee ball valves can be used on potable water?

Choose a valve listed as low lead in the product title, such as the UPBA-480B press ball valves in low lead bronze. Valves without that wording are intended for hydronic, steam and other non-potable service unless the product page says otherwise.

Thermostats for furnaces, boilers, heat pumps and electric heat, mostly Honeywell Home models made by Resideo, with tekmar and DiversiTech. A thermostat listed under its Resideo number, such as TH6220U2000, is the same part sold as the Honeywell Home T6 Pro.

The low-voltage lines include the T6 Pro (programmable, up to 3 heat/2 cool on heat pumps, with Wi-Fi, Z-Wave and hydronic versions), the FocusPRO N100 non-programmable, P200 programmable and S200 Wi-Fi models, the VisionPRO 8000 with RedLINK, the PRO 1000, 2000 and 3000, the T1 Pro, T3 Pro and T4 Pro and the FocusPRO 5000 and 6000. Some models in these lines have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status and replacement. The collection also holds line voltage, millivolt and mechanical heat-only thermostats, Southwire thermostat wire, guards, cover plates and remote sensors.

How to choose

  • Voltage: gas furnaces, heat pumps, boilers and air handlers use a 24 V thermostat powered by the equipment transformer. Electric baseboard, convectors and fan-forced wall heaters use a line voltage thermostat that switches 120 V or 240 V directly. The two are not interchangeable. A standing-pilot wall heater or gas fireplace with no transformer needs a 750 mV (millivolt) model such as the TS812A1007.
  • Conventional or heat pump, and stages: product titles give both ratings, for example "up to 2 Heat/1 Cool heat pump, 1 Heat/1 Cool conventional". The thermostat must cover at least as many stages as the equipment has; a heat pump with auxiliary heat counts as 2 heat.
  • C-wire: Wi-Fi models need continuous 24 V from a common (C) wire. Where the cable has no spare conductor, the THP9045A1023 WireSaver adapter adds a common at the equipment.
  • Schedule: non-programmable models hold one setpoint; programmable models run 5-2, 5-1-1 or 7-day schedules.
  • Wi-Fi or RedLINK: Wi-Fi connects the thermostat to the router and a phone app. RedLINK is Resideo's wireless link between a thermostat and its own sensors, equipment interface modules and TrueZONE adapter.

Common questions

Are Honeywell Home and Resideo thermostats the same?

Yes. Resideo makes and supports the Honeywell Home line, so a Resideo part number such as TH6220WF2006 is the thermostat sold as the Honeywell Home T6 Pro Smart.

What replaces a discontinued Honeywell thermostat?

Match the system type, the heat and cool stages and the schedule type of the old model. The product page of a discontinued model shows its replacement. For older part numbers, start with the Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference.

Which thermostat wire is listed?

Southwire thermostat wire is listed in 18/2, 18/4, 18/5 and 18/6. Check the installation guide of the new thermostat for the conductors it needs.

Non-programmable thermostats hold one setpoint until someone changes it, with no schedule to set up. That suits rentals, commercial spaces with irregular hours, garages, workshops and anyone who wants a simple control. Most models here are Honeywell Home thermostats made by Resideo, with a few from DiversiTech.

The collection has three groups. Digital models: the FocusPRO N100, PRO 1000, PRO 3000, T1 Pro, T3 Pro and FocusPRO 5000. Some models in these lines have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status and replacement. Mechanical models: the round T87N for 1 heat/1 cool and the T822, T827 and T834 for heat-only, cool-only or heat/cool systems. Special cases: the TS812A1007 for 750 mV millivolt heaters and FocusPRO RedLINK kits for TrueZONE panels. These are 24 V or millivolt controls; electric baseboard needs a line voltage thermostat instead.

How to choose

  • Heat-only or heat/cool: a heat-only thermostat, such as the PRO 1000 TH1100DV1000 or the T822K1000, has no cooling terminal. A system with central air or a heat pump needs a heat/cool model.
  • Conventional or heat pump: a 1 Heat/1 Cool model runs a single-stage furnace and air conditioner, or a heat pump with no auxiliary heat. A heat pump with auxiliary heat needs a 2 Heat/1 Cool heat pump model, such as the PRO 1000 TH1210DV1007, which has an emergency heat position.
  • Power and C-wire: mechanical T87 and T822 thermostats need no batteries and no C-wire. Digital models need power for the display, from batteries, from a common (C) wire, or either; check the power options on the product page.
  • Voltage: check that the system is 24 V. A standing-pilot wall heater or gas fireplace with no transformer is millivolt and needs a 750 mV model. Baseboard heat at 120 V or 240 V needs a line voltage thermostat.
  • Layout: PRO 1000 models come in horizontal (DH) and vertical (DV) cases. Pick the one that covers the marks left by the old thermostat, or add a cover plate.

Common questions

What is a non-programmable thermostat?

It holds one temperature until someone changes it, with no schedule to configure. It is a good fit for rentals, commercial spaces with irregular hours, garages and workshops.

Will a non-programmable thermostat work with a heat pump?

Only if the model is rated for heat pumps. A 1 Heat/1 Cool model covers a heat pump with no auxiliary heat. With auxiliary heat, choose a 2 Heat/1 Cool heat pump model and check that it has an emergency heat setting.

What replaces a discontinued non-programmable thermostat?

Match the heat and cool stages and the system type of the old thermostat. The product page of a discontinued model shows its replacement. The FocusPRO N100 is listed in 1 Heat/1 Cool, 2 Heat/1 Cool and 3 Heat/2 Cool versions. For older part numbers, see the Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference.

Programmable thermostats for 24 V forced air, heat pump and hydronic systems, in 5-2, 5-1-1 and 7-day schedules, from single-stage up to 3 heat/2 cool. Most are Honeywell Home models made by Resideo, with tekmar and DiversiTech.

The T6 Pro line covers most systems: TH6210U2001 for up to 2 heat/1 cool heat pump or 1 heat/1 cool conventional, TH6220U2000 for up to 2 heat/2 cool conventional, and TH6320U2008 for up to 3 heat/2 cool heat pump or 2 heat/2 cool conventional. The TH6100AF2004 is a heat-only hydronic version with a floor sensor input, and the TH6320ZW2003 adds Z-Wave. The collection also has the FocusPRO P200, the VisionPRO 8000 with RedLINK, the PRO 2000, the T4 Pro and the FocusPRO 6000. Some models in these lines have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status and replacement.

How to choose

  • Stages and system type: match the heat and cool stages in the product title to the equipment, and check both the heat pump rating and the conventional rating.
  • Schedule type: a 5-2 schedule has one program for weekdays and one for the weekend, 5-1-1 separates Saturday and Sunday, and 7-day sets each day on its own. The T6 Pro hydronic model lists 7-day, 5-1-1, 5-2 or non-programmable operation.
  • Power: T6 Pro specifications list a 20 to 30 Vac supply, and the TH6210U2001, TH6220U2000 and TH6320U2008 are listed as battery or hardwired. Check the power method on the product page.
  • Wall plate: the TH6210U2001, TH6220U2000 and TH6320U2008 mount on the UWP mounting system and are listed with a J-box adapter and a small decorative cover plate.

Common questions

Which schedule type do I need?

Choose 5-2 if weekdays are alike and both weekend days are alike, 5-1-1 if Saturday and Sunday differ, and 7-day if every day has a different routine.

Which programmable thermostat works with a heat pump?

Check the heat pump stage rating in the title. The T6 Pro TH6210U2001 and TH6220U2000 handle up to 2 heat/1 cool heat pumps, which is one compressor stage plus auxiliary heat. The TH6320U2008 handles up to 3 heat/2 cool, for a two-stage compressor with auxiliary heat.

What replaces a discontinued programmable thermostat?

Match the stages and system type of the old model. The product page of a discontinued model shows its replacement. For older part numbers, see the Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference.

Body HTML:
Smart and connected thermostats from Honeywell Home (made by Resideo) and tekmar. Three kinds of connection appear in this collection. Wi-Fi models, such as the T6 Pro Smart TH6220WF2006 and the FocusPRO S200 TH2110WF4008, connect to the home router and a phone app. Z-Wave models, such as the T6 Pro Z-Wave, join a home automation hub. RedLINK models, such as the VisionPRO 8000 TH8110R1008, use Resideo's own wireless link to indoor and outdoor sensors and equipment interface modules.

The T6 Pro Smart is listed for up to 2 heat/1 cool heat pumps or 2 heat/2 cool conventional systems. The FocusPRO S200 TH2110WF4008 is a 1 heat/1 cool model. The collection also lists the T10 Pro and T10+, the WiFi 9000 color touchscreen and Prestige IAQ kits. Some models in these lines have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status and replacement. The tekmar 564 is a Wi-Fi enabled 2 heat/1 cool/1 fan thermostat.

How to choose

  • C-wire first: Wi-Fi thermostats need continuous 24 V from a common (C) wire to run the display and radio. If the cable has no spare conductor, add a C-wire adapter at the equipment or pull new cable.
  • Stages and system type: match the heat pump or conventional stage rating in the title to the equipment, including auxiliary heat on a heat pump.
  • Type of connection: choose Wi-Fi for app control through the home router, Z-Wave if the home already has a Z-Wave hub, and RedLINK when the job needs wireless room sensors, an outdoor sensor or a wireless equipment interface module.
  • What a kit includes: Kits bundle a thermostat with other parts, such as an equipment interface module or sensors. The product specifications list the parts in each kit and the parts needed but not included.

Common questions

Do smart thermostats need a C-wire?

Wi-Fi models do. They need continuous 24 V power, which a two-wire heat-only cable or a four-wire cable with no common cannot supply. See the guide to the thermostat C-wire for the options.

What is the difference between Wi-Fi and RedLINK?

Wi-Fi links the thermostat to the home router and the phone app. RedLINK is Resideo's wireless link between the thermostat and its own accessories, such as indoor and outdoor sensors and equipment interface modules, sold in RedLINK accessories.

Will a smart thermostat work with a heat pump?

Yes, if its heat pump stage rating covers the system. The T6 Pro Smart TH6220WF2006 is listed for up to 2 heat/1 cool heat pumps, which is one compressor stage plus auxiliary heat. The heat pump thermostat guide explains the terminals.

Line voltage thermostats switch electric baseboard heaters, convectors, fan-forced heaters and floor heating directly at 120, 208 or 240 V, with no transformer or relay in between. They are not interchangeable with 24 V thermostats. The models here are Honeywell Home and Resideo.

The T410 and T498 are electric heat thermostats for baseboard heaters. Some T498 models have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status. Electronic models include the TL7235 non-programmable double-pole thermostat for 208/240 V, the TL8130 single-pole and TL8230 double-pole 7-day programmable thermostats, the TH114 manual and TH115 7-day programmable series, and the TH401 and TH450 manual thermostats with TRIAC switching. For electric floor heating, the TH115-AF-GA is a 7-day programmable floor thermostat for 120/240 V, rated 15 A, with a 5 mA GFCI.

How to choose

  • Supply voltage: check the voltage of the heater circuit. The TH401 and TH450 are listed for 120, 208 and 240 V, while the TL7235, TL8130 and TL8230 are listed for 208 and 240 V.
  • Single-pole or double-pole: a double-pole (DPST) thermostat breaks both legs of a 240 V circuit and gives a true off position. A single-pole (SPST) model breaks one leg, so the heater stays connected to power when the thermostat is off.
  • Load: add up the wattage of every heater on the thermostat and compare it with the thermostat's rating at your voltage. The TL7235 and TL8230 are listed at 15 A maximum, which is 3,600 W at 240 V.
  • Heater type: the specifications list the heaters each model is made for. The TL7235, TL8130 and TL8230 list electric baseboards, convectors and fan-forced heaters (resistive loads). Floor heating needs a floor heating thermostat such as the TH115-AF-GA.
  • Manual or programmable: manual models hold one setpoint; the TH115, TL8130 and TL8230 run 7-day schedules.

Common questions

What is a line voltage thermostat?

It switches a 120 V or 240 V electric heater directly, with no transformer. It is used for electric baseboard, convectors, fan-forced wall heaters and electric floor heat.

Single-pole or double-pole: which do I need?

A double-pole thermostat breaks both legs of a 240 V circuit and gives a true off position; a single-pole thermostat breaks one leg. Replace the old thermostat with the same type, and follow the manufacturer instructions and local electrical code.

Can I use a 24 V or smart thermostat on baseboard heat?

Not directly. A 24 V thermostat needs an electric heat relay with a transformer between it and the heater; see relays.

Body HTML:
Accessories for Honeywell Home and Resideo thermostats. Cover plates hide the paint line and screw holes left when a smaller thermostat replaces a larger one; they are made for a specific series, such as the 50002883-001 for FocusPRO and PRO models, the 50022893-001 for PRO TH1000 and TH2000 thermostats and the THP2400A1019 for the RedLINK VisionPRO.

TG511 medium and TG512 large universal thermostat guards are locking covers that stop tampering in public and commercial spaces; 191990A replacement keys fit the TG509 to TG512 guards. The THP9045A1023 WireSaver is a C-wire adapter for Wi-Fi thermostats and RedLINK 8000 series models. Remote sensors include the C7189U1005 indoor temperature sensor and the C7089U1006 outdoor temperature sensor.

How to choose

  • Thermostat series: cover plates and wall plates fit one series. Match the series named in the product title to the model number on the back of the thermostat body.
  • Plate size: measure the mark on the wall. The plate has to be larger than the old thermostat's outline; sizes are in the titles, for example 7-7/8 x 5-1/2 in for the 32003796-001.
  • Guard size: a guard must clear the thermostat on all sides and in depth. TG511 is the medium size and TG512 the large; clear versions let the display be read.
  • Sensor compatibility: a remote sensor works only with thermostats that have a sensor input for it. Check the thermostat's installation guide for the sensor part number it accepts.
  • C-wire adapter: the WireSaver is listed for Wi-Fi thermostats and RedLINK 8000 series models. Confirm that the thermostat and equipment are covered before ordering.

Common questions

Which cover plate fits my thermostat?

Cover plates are made for a thermostat series, so match the series in the product title, such as PRO, FocusPRO, VisionPRO or Prestige. Several T6 Pro thermostats are listed with a small decorative cover plate included.

What if my wall has no C-wire?

A C-wire adapter such as the THP9045A1023 WireSaver adds a common at the equipment so a Wi-Fi thermostat can be powered without pulling new cable. The other option is new thermostat wire with a spare conductor.

What is a thermostat guard for?

It is a locking cover that goes over the thermostat so that only someone with the key can change the setting. Guards are common in offices, schools, rentals and shared spaces.
